title: Context Anchoring Notes for Small PRs
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight personal scratchpad for anchoring reviewer context on small, high-risk PRs (1-4 files, touch hotpath). The goal is to make reviews faster and safer by: (1) surfacing intent; (2) listing quick local repro steps; (3) small microbench ideas to validate perf regressions; (4) explicit follow-ups for rollout/observability.

When to use this note:
- I’m about to open a PR that changes request routing, KV cache behavior, or batching heuristics.
- Patch modifies anything on the token emission path or request lifecycle.

Quick high-level blurb to paste into PR description (copy/paste):
- Intent: reduce tail latency for short-sequence chat by skipping prefix-cache when prefix length < 32 tokens.
- Surface risk: may increase token compute for workloads with lots of tiny prefix re-use.
- Sanity checks included: unit test for cache bypass, added e2e with prefix fixture.
- Perf delta: local smoke shows 6% wall-clock improvement on toy 1k qps microbench (needs CI/infra validation).

Checklist for reviewers (short):
- [ ] Read the short blurb above before diving into diffs.
- [ ] Verify unit test covers bypass branch and fallback.
- [ ] Confirm no change to persisted cache format (migration-free).
- [ ] Look for non-obvious concurrency races in cache update path.
- [ ] Check that telemetry increments for bypass are attached to the same metric family (no new metric drift).

Local repro / smoke commands (devbox):
- Start local server: ./dev/run_local.sh --devices=1 --env=dev
- Run microbench (python): python infra/microbench/token-emitter.py --qps 200 --seq 16 --jobs 8 --warmup 5 --duration 30 --endpoint http://localhost:8080/generate
- Collect flamegraphs: ./scripts/collect-flame.sh 8080 out.svg (requires flameprof in PATH)
- Quick curl example to hit bypass path:
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","prefix_tokens":10,"max_tokens":4}' | jq .latency

Microbench plan (minimal):
- Baseline: master at commit abc123 - run emitter for seq=16, seq=128, seq=512. Capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Change: this branch - same runs.
- Compare: look for regression in seq=128 where bypass shouldn't help. Expect improvement in seq=16.
- Quick stats I capture in the PR: p50_delta, p99_delta, cpu%_delta.

Small safety matrix (if rollout):
- Canary: enable feature flag on 2% of production traffic for 24h. Alert if p99 increases >5% or errors >0.2%.
- Fallback: revert flag to off, auto-fall back to cached-path within 2 minutes.
- Telemetry hooks: metric.cache.bypass.count, metric.cache.hits, metric.cache.misses, metric.request.latency.p99-tagged.

Potential gotchas & hypotheses to test (notes to self):
- Hypothesis A: short sequences with repeated prompts still benefit, but repeated tiny prefixes across sessions may pay cost of extra comp. Need to test session-local cache behavior.
- Hypothesis B: disabling prefix caching for prefixes < 32 tokens will shift load to kernel that does more attention compute per-token; watch GPU memory churn and kernel selection logs.
- Edge: a race where two concurrent requests both decide to bypass and both write to the same cache slot — ensure conditional write is still atomic.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
1) Add a small regression test that replays a 5-user session for 1 minute and asserts p99 stays within threshold. (owner: Asha)
2) Add a quick dashboard tile under /console/latency/short-seq to track p50/p99 for seq<=32. (owner: Theo)
3) Write a short note in runbook about the flag and rollback steps. (owner: Kai)

Reviewer heuristics (how I want feedback):
- Exact code correctness bits: comment inline on the line.
- Design/architecture: summarize as a one-paragraph comment or push to a short GH discussion.
- If you suspect perf/usability issues, drop a short reproduction note or ask for the microbench run from CI.

Random TODOs (if I forget):
- grep for other places that compute prefix length; consolidate helper.
- Consider adding a config knob for minimum prefix tokens (default 32).
- Clean up temporary debug logs added in 3 files before merge.

Notes about tests included in the branch:
- unit/cache_bypass_test.py: asserts bypass branch chosen, verifies no cache mutation when flagged.
- integration/short_seq_e2e.yaml: small local harness using sample fixture. Not yet run in CI due to infra queue.

Questions to ask on review if you’re lazy (copy into PR comment):
- Does the bypass metric tag align with existing telemetry conventions? If not, suggest rename.
- Any concerns about concurrency model here? I tried to keep writes CAS-style but would appreciate a race read.

References and links I check before merging:
- Prior PR for cache eviction logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4392
- Observability guideline: CONFLUENCE-OBS-07

End of scratchpad. Keep this short blurb at the top of PR and delete the TODOs before finalizing.
